title: corerules Content Pack, format version 0.1
description: Canonical schema, authored by the corpus-v1 map (ticket 05 spine, ticket 14 shapes). Covers the ten kinds the proving slice needs, not all 27. Enforcement is two-tiered: what is declared here, and what the validator checks. Recursive structures, numeric ranges and cross-field rules are the validator's.

id.description: Pack-scoped, opaque, derived from the source anchor (ticket 07). '#n' discriminates records sharing one source file.

provenance.description: Ticket 05: replaces §7.1's book-and-page, which this corpus cannot supply. 'section' is for a human holding the printed book; 'anchor' is for the machine, and is what the id derives from.

interpretation.description: Ticket 11: the book is ambiguous and this record is a reading. Absent means the source was unambiguous — never that nobody looked.

scalar.description: Ticket 06: the only scalars a predicate or operand may name. 'level' is ALWAYS qualified by class — the unqualified form does not exist, because §6.1's sum type means Fighter 5 / Mage 4 has no 'level 5'.

dice.description: Ticket 15 decision 1, implemented here by ticket 13 finding 42 — the decision was settled and the schema had no pattern at all. A §3.3 VALUE TYPE: no id, never referenced by `record`. Not yet referenced by any kind either, because the kinds that carry dice (generation methods, wealth options) are outside the proving slice. The decision states the grammar as 'NdM+-k'. Measured over the v1 RTF: 2,574 notations, of which 77.9% are NdM and 17.4% NdM+-k — and 4.7% (121) are NdM x k, which that grammar REJECTS. So the multiplier is admitted. A bare 'd10' with no count is admitted for the same reason: the corpus writes it. WIDENED by finding 79: the first pattern assumed the grammar 'NdM [xK] [±J]' in that order, and the corpus also writes '(NdM ± J) x K' — 14 occurrences including the wizard's standard starting money, '(1d4+1) x 10 gp'. Grouping changes the arithmetic, so this is not a notation variant but a different expression, and the first pattern silently rejected it.

operand.description: Ticket 15: known unknown #4 fired — 31 corpus occurrences of halving, division and rounding inside kit effects. NOT a seventh operation: 'adjust' still sums, only its operand widens. Used by effects AND by predicate values, since the arithmetic appears on both sides. WIDENED by ticket 13 finding 110: a fourth arm for `N on 1dM`, which is a value the corpus states directly and no arithmetic over integers can recover.

computedOperand.description: Closed set, not general arithmetic. Rounding is a property of the operand — which is where §7.2's requirement finally lands.

condition.description: Ticket 06: a closed, flat vocabulary — compare, member, has. Race lists are membership and unless/except are §4.3's 'except'. Boolean combination lives one level up in 'clause', never here: a condition is a leaf, which is what keeps the evaluator a loop instead of a recursive descent.

clause.description: Ticket 13 finding 10, repairing ticket 06. Disjunction was measured at 4 occurrences by a regex that required '<Ab> N ... or ... <Ab>'; the corpus writes '<Ab> or <Ab> N', which occurs 38 times, and four v1 kits need it: the Homesteader and Bandit as 'A and (B or C)', the Goblinsticker and Smuggler as a bare 'A or B'. So a clause is a condition or a disjunction of conditions, and NOTHING ELSE: one level, no recursion, no 'or' of 'and'. Both corpus examples are that shape, and it keeps the evaluator flat, which is what ticket 06 was actually defending. Negation is still absent — finding 7's 33 occurrences remain text.

predicate.description: A flat list of clauses; every clause must hold. Ticket 13 finding 10 widened the entries from conditions to clauses, so a single entry may be a disjunction.

effect.description: §4.3's six operations as a discriminated union, so an operation carrying the wrong fields is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely invalid — §5's 'illegal states are unrepresentable', and §6.1's principle: structural for model incoherence, pack-declared for game rules. Ticket 13 finding 108: an effect may carry its own `provenance`. A record's effects are not necessarily all from one book — `phb:dwarf` is the PHB's record and 28 of its effects are the Complete Book of Dwarves re-scoring the PHB's proficiencies. Without this the pack asserts that the core rules say something they do not.

text.description: §4.3: anything outside the vocabulary is carried as text and not computed.

record.description: What every pack kind carries. Value types (§3.3) deliberately do NOT reference this: they have no id, which is how §3's three-way split is enforced structurally.

attachable.description: §4.1: ONE closed shape used three times. Kit, Deity and Subrace each extend this and add only their target and cardinality — the two things §4.1 says they cannot share. Expressed structurally so that if the claim is wrong, it breaks here rather than after transcription.

effectsModelled.description: Ticket 13, found by running the extractor: without this, a mechanically extracted record with `effects: []` validates as a COMPLETE record with no effects. That is A3's own distinction — 'does not restrict' versus 'not transcribed yet' — missing one level down. §5.1 put it on the pack; a record needs it too, because extraction produces the incomplete state by construction and the corpus lives in it for years. Declared rather than inferred, exactly as A3 is.

tableAxis.description: How one axis of a table is keyed. Ticket 13's resolution of known unknown #2 found the axes HETEROGENEOUS: Table 26 keys on a thieving skill (an id), Table 28 on a Dexterity score (an integer), and Table 30 on a level BAND ('1-4', '5-8'). One kind would have fitted none of them.

vocabulary.description: Required when kind is 'id': which enumeration the keys are drawn from, so the checker can refuse an unknown one.

tableValue.description: Ticket 13 finding 71: the Swashbuckler 'fights with the THAC0 of a FIGHTER of his experience level' — an effect that must READ a table belonging to another class. Names the field the table supplies, whose context it belongs to, and the index to read it at.

of.description: Whose table — a class entry, usually another class than the character's.

definition.description: Ticket 13 finding 101: a kit's named benefits and hindrances are things the kit BRINGS INTO BEING — 227 of them across 346 records, and 216 used exactly once, by the record that invented them. Given an id they are 216 references that can never resolve, because there is nothing to point at and nothing to transcribe: the definition IS the kit's own field. So the definition lives in the effect that grants it. The eleven used by more than one record are a different thing and keep their ids.

text.description: What the source says it does, in the source's words.

rollUnder.description: Ticket 13 finding 110. The demihuman detection abilities are all ONE shape — `1-5 on 1d6`, `1-7 on 1d10`, `1 on 1d6` — and the pack had nowhere to put it: `operand` was integer, computedOperand or tableValue, and `dice` was a value type NOTHING referenced (finding 42 said so and could not say why). A chance is not a number the corpus prints; writing 83% where the book writes `1-5 on 1d6` is inference, which A3 forbids. So the operand widens to hold the roll the book actually specifies, and `dice` finally has a consumer. 17 occurrences across the six player races; none in 1,121 kit effects, because kit bonuses are flat modifiers.

rollAtMost.description: Success on this result or lower. `1-5 on 1d6` is 5.

provenanceMode.description: Ticket 12: §5.1 says the house-rule escape hatch IS the pack, so provenance cannot be unconditionally mandatory. Declared rather than inferred — A3 applied to provenance.

sources.description: Ticket 05: which source bytes this pack came from. Ticket 02 established that 'the DMG' is ambiguous with two byte-different variants in circulation.

declares.description: A3 (§5.1). Rule-set names are the Engine's closed enumeration — §3.4's single exception to open enumerations. Declarations scope to the subjects this pack introduces; the Engine unions them.

files.description: §7.1: declaration over discovery. A file present but unlisted is reported.

target.description: §4.1: a class entry, or the race.
§4.1: the race. §3.1: a Subrace is a Race with a parent reference.

items.description: Ticket 13 finding 107. §3.1 already says a Subrace IS a Race with a parent reference, and a Subrace is one of §4.1's three Attachable arms — so a Race carrying effects is not a new idea, it is the same idea the schema never granted the parent. A Race has NO target and NO prerequisite: it is not attached to a character, it is one of the things a character is.

isGroup.description: Table 44 prints `Bow`, `Crossbow` and `Sword` as headings over their variants, scoring nothing. The kits reference the GROUP far more often than a variant, so groups are records too — and this flag is what keeps a group from looking like a weapon with no cost and no damage.

cost.description: As printed: '5 gp', '3sp/12'. Money is not an integer in this book.

damageType.description: P, S, B, or a combination.

items.description: Ticket 14 declared this kind with NO fields, before anything was transcribed. Its shape is Table 44's columns, set in session 51 the same way the nonweapon proficiency's four fields turned out to be Table 37's four columns — the book's own table IS the record shape.

group.description: Ticket 13 session 50: ticket 14 gave this kind a SINGLE group, written before anything was transcribed. PHB Table 37 puts 15 of its 65 proficiencies in TWO groups — a group is the list a class may buy from at normal cost, so belonging to two is what a crossover IS, not an anomaly. Widened to an array.

abilityCheck.description: A `scalar`, not a bare id. Absent for the two proficiencies Table 37 scores `NA` — Blind-fighting and Mountaineering have no ability check at all. Absent also where the book scores the ABILITY as special, as Intimidation does: 'ability special, special modifier'.

modifier.description: Ticket 13 finding 104: five Complete Thief's proficiencies score 'special modifiers' rather than a number — the modifier depends on circumstances the description sets out. Absent where a table scores NA; `special` where the book says so; an integer otherwise. The three states are different and the format now keeps them apart.

lookupTables.description: §3.1: named, typed table. XP progressions, THAC0, saving-throw matrices and thieving-skill adjustments are instances of it, owned by their class, group or race.

supplies.description: Ticket 13 finding 20 and its resolution: a table had an id derived from its source FILE, a name §7.3 says is never identity, and nothing saying what it was a table OF — so the Engine could not find the one it needed. It now names the FIELD PATH it fills, in the same vocabulary the effects use: a table supplying `thiefSkill` answers for `thiefSkill.openLocks`. Chosen over a second closed enumeration so that §3.4 keeps its single exception. Tables that supply no field — a list of permitted weapons, say — carry no `supplies` and the Engine does not consume them, which is A3's distinction applied to tables.

columnsAre.description: Present when the COLUMNS are a second axis rather than plain headings — Table 27 is (skill x race), Table 28 its transpose.

spheres.description: Ticket 13 finding 99: 64 reference occurrences pointed at priest SPHERES and no kind held them. A sphere is a named category a spell belongs to — the priest's side of what a school is for a wizard, and the two are the same shape used twice, exactly as §4.1's three Attachable arms are.

spellSchools.description: The wizard's side of the same shape. See `spheres`.

spells.description: Only the spells the pack REFERENCES are transcribed — twelve of the PHB's several hundred. A3 makes that legitimate rather than incomplete: the manifest declares what the pack covers, and a spell nobody grants is not a debt.

armor.description: From Table 46's Armor Class Ratings. The table rates COMBINATIONS — 'leather or padded + shield' — so only the items the pack cites are recorded, at the rating the table gives them alone.

grantedAbilities.description: The eleven abilities used by MORE THAN ONE record. Everything used once is defined inline by the effect that grants it (`defines`, finding 101); these eleven are shared, and several are not kit inventions at all but CLASS abilities that kits reference — `phb:bard-spellcasting` is cited by three bard kits that take it away.

alignments.description: Ticket 13 finding 113. The last of finding 99's four homeless kinds — alignments, spheres, schools of magic and armour — and the one the corpus points at hardest: 49 of the pack's 166 unresolved reference occurrences. A closed list of nine, and NOT a flat one. The PHB opens the chapter by saying alignment 'is divided into two sets of attitudes: order and chaos, and good and evil', and that the nine are what COMBINING them produces — so the record carries the two axes, not just the label. An alignment has no effects: nothing in the PHB's chapter is a mechanic, which is why the kind has a shape and no `effects` array.
